J U D G M E N T :

1. Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the present appeal, challenging the order dated 10.12.2018 ("the impugned order" in FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 1 of 11 short) of Ld.
Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate, Jam Nagar House, New Delhi ("ADM" in short), whereby he imposed penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ (Rupees one lac only) upon the appellant under Section 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ("FSS Act" in short), for selling misbranded product in contravention to Sections 23, 26(1), 26(2)(ii), 27(1) & 27(2)(C) of FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) of FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labeling), Regulations, 2011 {FSS(FPS & FA) Regulations in short}.
2.

sentences.text:
Briefly stating, the facts as per the appeal are that on 24.10.2016, a sample of "Pan Masala" was lifted by the Food Safety Officer (in short FSO) from the premises of Food Business Operator ("FBO"
in short) Sh. Prem Chand Jain S/o Late Sh. Nemi Chand Jain, M/s Jain Book Corner and Jain Tobacconist, 42, Bengali Market, New Delhi.

The sample was divided into four equal parts and one Sh. Sunil Kumar vs The State (Food Safety Officer) on 11 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97113668/
1 counterpart was sent to Food Analyst, Delhi.

On analysis by the Food Analyst, Delhi, the said sample was declared to be misbranded vide report dt.28.10.2016 as the complete address of the manufacturer was not declared as required under Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (FPS & FA)
Regulations.
Consequently, a complaint was filed against the appellantherein by the FSO before FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 2 of 11 the Adjudicating Officer.

sentences.text: After pleadings and enquiry, the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order dated 10.12.2018 imposing a penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ upon the appellant.

3. The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter alia on the grounds among others that Ld.
ADM has failed to appreciate that the company manufacturer of the sampled commodity has not been arrayed as accused/one of the respondents.

The appellant has neither supplied the sampled commodity nor has any business dealings with respondent no. 1 to 3 and that Sh. Prem Chand Jain,
the Business Operator has clearly mentioned in his reply that the sample commodity was purchased from the market through selling agent Sh. Krishan Kumar, but he has never visited premises of the company and Sh. Prem Chand Jain replied to the FSO during investigation that the sample commodity was purchased from the market and no bill was issued on demand.
Therefore, the appellant has no concern with the sample commodity and unnecessarily has been penalized by the Ld. ADM.
Nobody can be prosecuted merely on the label declaration in the absence of purchased bill, invoice, purchased memorandum etc.

In the present case, the manufacturer has mentioned the address of registered office on the sample commodity as 52/34, Naya Ganj, Kanpur208001 and by writing registered office, address is the complete address.
FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 3 of 11 4.

sentences.text: The Ld. Chief PP for the State has not filed reply to the appeal, however, he has opposed the appeal.

5. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the appellant and Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State and have perused the records and also gone through the judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant and Ld. Chief PP for the State.

6. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant argued that as per the Food Analyst report dated 28.10.2016,
there is no food adulteration.
There is an allegation by the respondent that complete address was not mentioned on the label of the sampled commodity.
Respondent no.1 to 3 were the FBOs and penalty of Rs.50,000/ each was imposed upon them.
Whereas, the appellant herein was the nominee of the manufacturer company and penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ was imposed upon him.
"Pan Masala" was purchased from the market.
No name of appellant is mentioned either on the panchnama or on form VA.
The appellant is not aware who is Krishan Kumar and why the appellant has been impleaded in this case.
Mere label declaration is not sufficient for prosecution.

When purchase bill is not there then why the appellant has been impleaded as a respondent before the Ld.
ADM.
There is no liability of any employee without impleading company and the main culprit is company.
Further, if fine is imposed, the same may be recovered from the company.
There are FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 4 of 11 the requirements on the label i.e. name of the manufacturer, city and pin code number.

sentences.text: Ld. Chief PP for the State/respondent has argued that the present case pertains to label declaration.
The present case is for violation of Regulation 2.2.2.6.
Only brand name and Delhi has been mentioned on the label.
It did not disclose the complete/exact address of Delhi.
As per combined reading of Section 25 & 26 of FSS Act, a joint liability can be fastened upon both the manufacturer company as well as on its nominee.
The defect is apparent.
The sample collected pertains to the appellant.
Further, there is no complaint that there is any fake material / item of the appellant in the market.
There is no denial that items do not concern with the appellant.
Main duty of the analyzer is to examine the sample.
This case is of "misbrand" only about label.

The FBO,
supplier, manufacturer, nominee are liable in the case of Misbrand and in this case, the appellant is the nominee of the manufacturing unit.
The appellant is therefore, liable as per Section 27 of FSS Act.
The rules and regulations of old Food Adulteration Act cannot be applied since new Act has come in the year 2006.
The standards and parameters, which have been laid down by the legislature are to be followed but the appellant has not followed it for selling the Pan Masala in this case.
The appellant did FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 6 of 11 not comply with the standards of rules / regulations of Food Safety and Standard Act.

sentences.text: 8. In the present case, the appellant has challenged the impugned order dt.10.12.2018 mainly on the grounds that the appellant cannot be penalised for the offence of misbranding in the absence of purchased bill, invoice, purchased memorandum etc.

The manufacturer has mentioned the address on the sample commodity as "M/s Ashok & Co.  Pan Bahar Ltd., New Delhi110015.
9.

The Food Analyst vide his report dated 28.10.2016 opined the sample as misbranded as the same was without declaration of complete address of manufacturer being in violation of Regulation Sh. Sunil Kumar vs The State (Food Safety Officer) on 11 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97113668/
3 2.2.2.6(i) of the FSS (P&L) Regulation, 2011.
10. Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (P&L) Regulations reads as under : 2.2.2(6)  Labelling of Pre packaged Foods FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 7 of 11 (i) Name and complete address of the manufacturer The name and complete address of the manufacturer and the manufacturing unit if these are located at different places and in case the manufacturer is not the packer or bottler, the name and complete address of the packing or bottling unit as the case may be shall be declared on every package of food;
11.
It would be pertinent to mention here that Section 23(1) FSS Act requires that no one shall manufacture, distribute, sell any packaged food products which is not labelled as per regulations.

Section 23(1) reads as under: "23. Packaging and labelling of foods.(1) No person shall manufacture, distribute, sell or expose for sale or despatch or deliver to any agent or broker for the purpose of sale, any packaged food products which are not marked and labelled in the manner as may be specified by regulations:
Provided that the labels shall not contain any statement, claim, design or device which is false or misleading in any particular concerning the food products contained in the package or concerning the quantity or the nutritive value implying medicinal or therapeutic claims or in relation to the place of origin of the said food products."
12.
Further, such noncompliance renders a packaged food article misbranded in terms of Section 3(1)(zf)(c)(i) of FSS Act.

26.Responsibilities of the Food business operator.

(ii)which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter; or"
14. Section 27(3)(c) FSS Act fastens liability for sale etc. of misbranded food article.

Said provision reads as under: "27. Liability of the Manufacturers, packers,
wholesalers, distributors and sellers. .....

(3)The seller shall be liable under this Act, for any article of food which is .....

15. The appellant himself admitted vide his letter dated 18.10.2017 addressed to Sh. Hukam Singh,
Food Safety Officer, as the nominee of M/s Ashok & Co.  Pan Bahar Ltd. at the time of lifting the sample and even continued thereafter.

The appellant also enclosed photocopy of his nomination by the company in his favour under Food Safety & Standards Rule, 2011 - Form No. IX (Form of Nomination - Refer Rule 2.5.1) Nomination of persons by a company.
Therefore, in view of the above provisions of law, the appellant being the nominee is liable for manufacturing/sale/supply of misbranded sample food article.
FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 9 of 11 16.

sentences.text:
From the above, it is clear that the declaration 'name and complete address of the manufacturer'
was required to be put on the label, in terms of Regulations 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (P&L) Regulations.

17. Perusal of the record of Ld. ADM reveals that the Form VA prepared by the FSO declares as under :
"MFD BY : ASHOK & CO.  PAN BAHAR LTD, NEW DELHI110015 REGD. OFFICE : 52/34, NAYA GANJ, KANPUR208001 CONSUMER CARE EXECUTIVE NO. 011 25173859"
18.
From the above declaration it is evident that the label does not mention the 'complete address of the manufacturer'.

Thus, the label on sample commodity violates Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (P&L)
Regulations, violation of the same amounts to misbranding in terms of section 3(1)(zf) r/w section 26(2)(ii), 27(1) & 27(2) of FSS Act.
Misbranding is punishable under section 52 FSS Act with a penalty of Rs. 3,00,000/.
Whereas, the Ld. ADM has imposed only a consolidated penalty of Rs.1,00,000/ on the appellant.

19. In view of the above facts and circumstances, arguments on behalf of the parties and the materials available on reocrd and also the judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant and the Ld. Chief PP for the State, I am of the considered opinion that the FSAT No. 04/19 Sh. Sunil Kumar vs. FSO Page No. 10 of 11 sample food article i.e. "Pan Masala" did not conform to the specified standard as laid down in Regulation 2.2.2.6(i) of FSS (P&L) Regulations.
Non conforming to the specified standard rendered the sample i.e. Pan Masala as misbranded in terms of Section 3(1)(zf) of the FSS Act.
The parameters and standards laid down by the legislatures were not followed by the appellant for selling the Pan Masala.
The judgments relied upon by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant are not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
Thus, the appellant has failed to demonstrate any justified reason to interfere with the impugned order dt.10.12.2018 of the Ld. ADM.
Section 52 of FSS Act prescribes a maximum penalty of Rs.3,00,000/ (Rupees Three Lacs only).

However, the Ld. ADM imposed a consolidated penalty of Rs.1,00,000 lacs upon the appellant which is only 1/3rd amount of the penalty of Rs. 3,00,000/
prescribed under Section 52 FSS Act.
Accordingly, this appeal is devoid of any merits and the same is dismissed.
Copy of this Judgment along with the record of the Ld. ADM be sent to the Ld. ADM.
